The fault chain: likely cause → mechanism → fault. Each link shows its own evidence and confidence.
Not measurable directly. Pointed to by: lead hip
turned 31° at impact vs ~45° typical.

(threshold 4%). Key frames: address + impact.

Verified by the rule table. Drill and mobility

confidence:
high
Here’s what the video shows. From address to impact your hips move
toward the ball by 7% of your body height. Up to 4% is normal; past that,
the rule table calls it early extension, and in your clip it’s clear. The
most likely reason is that your lead hip doesn’t turn enough — 31° at
impact, where about 45° is typical — so your hips slide toward the ball
instead of rotating. That part is an inference, so it’s marked medium.
It may feel like you stay down, but at impact your hips have moved
toward the ball. For the rest of this bucket, do the wall drill. Between
sessions, the 90/90 hip rotation helps the hip turn.
Set up with your backside touching a wall
(or golf bag). Make slow half swings,
keeping your trail glute on the wall
through impact.

g.text: Fixes: hips move toward the ball

text.tspan: Sit with both knees bent at 90°, one in
front, one to the side. Rotate to switch
sides without using your hands.
Generic guidance, not medical advice — see a
physiotherapist if you feel pain.

about this result: Early extension · 11 Nov

text.tspan: Answers are based only on this analysis. No
new faults, numbers or drills.
I’ve looked at your 7-iron from 11 Nov.
Ask me anything about this result.
Why does it feel like I’m staying down
when I’m not?
Your chest stays bent over, so staying
down is what you feel. The impact frame
shows something else: your hips are 7% of
your body height closer to the ball than at
address — the limit is 4%.
Can I do this drill in a net?
Yes. The wall drill doesn’t need ball
flight. If there’s no wall, use your golf
bag: 3 × 10 slow half swings, trail glute
stays on the bag through impact.
And what about my grip?
This analysis doesn’t measure grip, so I
can’t tell you anything about it. Worth
confirming with a coach.

svg.text: How do I know the drill is working?
Is the posture thing a problem?
